GetExpiryTime dereferences entry.Attributes without a nil check; IsExpired guards it, direct callers must.
UpdateEntryWithResponse returns the response unexamined: UpdateEntryResponse carries no error code, so a failed condition shows up only as the gRPC error.

metadataEventMatchesPath matches every path when pathPrefix is empty (strings.HasPrefix with ""), whatever pathPrefixes or directories say; a subscription that means 'only these directories' must pass a non-empty prefix it never matches.
IsOlderDir counts a directory as old once its crtime is more than 3 seconds in the past.

weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.character: The FilerClient interface and the generic entry operations built on it: get, paginated list with a snapshot boundary, exists, mkdir, mkfile, remove
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.what: FilerClient is anything with WithFilerClient(streaming, fn), AdjustedUrl and GetDataCenter. GetEntry returns an entry with the log position and signature the filer stamped. ReadDirAllEntriesWithSnapshot pages a whole directory 10,000 entries at a time; the first page's snapshot_ts_ns (in a response, or in the stream trailer for an empty listing) is sent back on every later page so the whole walk reports one listing time, and a full page that does not advance its cursor is an error. DoSeaweedListWithSnapshot asks for limit+1 entries to know which one is last, holds each entry back one step so fn learns isLast, and carries OmitChunks from the context. Exists compares the entry's directory flag. Mkdir / MkdirExclusive (O_EXCL; a taken name is returned after the failover callback, so it is not counted against the filer) and MkFile build entries owned by the process uid/gid. Remove / DoRemoveRequest delete and treat a not-found answer as success.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.why: Consequence: a cache built from a listing (a mount's directory cache) must replay the metadata events that happened after the listing and only those, so it needs one listing time for the whole walk. Design: the filer only stamps and echoes that time (filer_grpc_server.go ListEntries passes nothing to the store), so later pages still read live data; the snapshot travels in a trailer for empty pages because older consumers would read a snapshot-only response as an entry. MkdirExclusive returns the collision outside the callback because failover helpers retry a callback error on the next filer.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.when: s3api (bucket and directory creation, listings, removes), shell commands, mounts, replication sinks and admin tools.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.ux: Consistent directory listings and idempotent deletes.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go.if_broken: Listings loop forever or drop entries; deletes fail on already-missing entries; exclusive creates are retried across filers until they appear to succeed.
gotchas: DoRemoveRequest treats any error whose text contains the not-found message as success and then returns a nil response; RemoveWithResponse callers must nil-check it.
MkFile and Mkdir stamp OS_UID/OS_GID of the calling process, not of an S3 identity.
A first listing that returns no entries and comes from a filer without the trailer reports snapshot 0, which callers such as CompleteDirectoryBuild read as 'no server snapshot' (author comment).

snapshot_ts_ns is not a store snapshot: the filer stamps time.Now() on the first page and echoes the caller's value afterwards, so entries created, renamed or deleted between pages can still be skipped or repeated.

weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_bfs.go.character: Client-side breadth-first tree walk and the consumer of the filer's server-side BFS metadata stream
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_bfs.go.what: TraverseBfs walks a tree with 5 workers sharing a queue: each worker lists one directory fully (ReadDirAllEntries), calls fn for every entry and enqueues subdirectories. A visited set drops a directory delivered twice, the first error cancels the walk and is returned, and idle workers poll the queue every 50 ms. StreamBfs reads a TraverseBfsMetadata stream and calls fn with each entry's directory, entry and per-path commit timestamp.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_bfs.go.why: Consequence: a directory listed twice (a page-boundary race with a concurrent rename, or a store whose order misbehaves) would make the walk re-list the same subtree, possibly without end. Design: a pending counter, not channel closure, decides when the walk is done, because workers both consume and produce work.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_bfs.go.when: TraverseBfs: shell and maintenance walks. StreamBfs: filer.go's metadata catch-up from a peer (loading a snapshot of another filer's tree).
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_bfs.go.if_broken: Tree walks hang, repeat subtrees or stop early without an error.
gotchas: StreamBfs's olderThanTsNs is only logged; it is not sent in the request, so any time filtering is up to fn.
fn runs concurrently from five goroutines and must be safe for that.

weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_dfs.go.character: A resumable depth-first tree walk that reports how far it got
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_dfs.go.what: TraverseDfs walks under a path in listing order, 1024 entries per page. Files before the next directory are passed to fn concurrently (up to 5 at a time, visitDfsRun), and progress receives each file only once every entry before it is done; a directory is reported after its whole subtree. Given resumeAfter (a path previously reported), the walk starts inclusively at each component of that path, skipping what was done and descending into the directory it stopped in. A full page that does not advance is an error.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_dfs.go.why: Consequence: a long metadata backup interrupted midway would otherwise start over. Design: depth-first in listing order makes one path a complete checkpoint: everything before it, and the subtree of a directory it names, is done.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_dfs.go.ux: A restarted filer.meta.backup resumes where it stopped.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client_dfs.go.if_broken: Backups restart from the beginning, skip entries after a resume, or hang on a store whose ordering does not advance.
gotchas: progress is called unconditionally; a nil progress callback panics.
fn may run concurrently for the files of one directory.

weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.character: A hand-written protobuf scanner that reads only the fields the subscription matcher needs from a logged metadata event
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.what: ScanMetadataEventSkeleton walks a marshaled SubscribeMetadataResponse with protowire and keeps directory, ts_ns and, from the event notification, the old and new entry names and new_parent_path, skipping every other field (chunk lists above all). It returns ok=false on any malformed input or on a repeated message field (which protobuf would merge), telling the caller to fall back to a full unmarshal. Entry names follow proto's last-occurrence-wins rule.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.why: Consequence: a metadata subscriber that watches one prefix makes the filer test every logged event against it; unmarshaling whole entries with their chunk lists just to read two names dominated that cost. Design: decode only the matcher's inputs, and fully decode only events that match.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.when: filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.go, when replaying persisted log entries for a subscription.
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.ux: Lower filer CPU for many narrow subscribers (mounts, S3 gateways).
weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_pb_event_scan.go.if_broken: Subscribers miss events (a field misread) or the filer burns CPU decoding every event in full.
gotchas: The skeleton's entries carry only names; nothing but the matcher may consume it, and a matching event must still be fully unmarshaled before it is sent.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.character: The filer's core gRPC handlers: entry lookup and listing, create/update/delete/append, ObjectTransaction and its batch, volume assignment and collections
weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.what: LookupDirectoryEntry reads through fencedFindEntry, which stamps a log position under the path's shared lock so the answer reflects every event at or below it. ListEntries streams StreamListDirectoryEntries pages up to the limit (default DirListingLimit), drops chunks for omit_chunks after stamping FileSize, sends a listing time (the caller's snapshot_ts_ns or now) on the first entry and in the trailer. CreateEntry, UpdateEntry and DeleteEntry first forward to the key's ring write owner when the request is exclusive or conditional (O_EXCL, WriteCondition, expected_extended), then take the per-path exclusive lock, stamp the log fence, evaluate preconditions on the current entry, diff chunks against the old entry (cleanupChunks: MinusChunks, CompactFileChunks to drop covered chunks, MaybeManifestize), apply the storage rule (read-only prefixes reject, rule TTL fills a missing one) and commit, deleting garbage chunks only after a successful write and returning the metadata event. ObjectTransaction forwards to the owner of route_key (one hop, is_moved), locks lock_key, replays a recorded outcome for a repeated request_id, checks the request condition (against condition_key, with the condition_alt_key fallback that resolves the latest version through the .versions pointer and treats a bare implicit directory as absent), then applies each mutation in order with its own optional condition: PUT, DELETE (optionally removing an emptied parent), PATCH_EXTENDED (set/remove keys, replace content, touch mtime) and RECOMPUTE_LATEST (applyRecomputeLatest: scan the directory, pick the first or last child by name, copy mapped keys, size, mtime and name into the pointer, demote the previous child). ObjectTransactionBatch runs independent transactions in sequence. AppendToEntry appends chunks at the current end under a cluster short-lived lock plus the path lock. AssignVolume resolves the path's storage rule and asks the master, returning the replica holders and the rule's fsync. Also LookupVolume, CollectionList, DeleteCollection.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.why: Consequence: the S3 gateway's conditional PUT, versioned writes, delete markers, multipart completion and object-lock guards all commit through these handlers, so their atomicity is the gateway's atomicity. Design: the store's insert is an upsert, so a check-then-write is only atomic under one lock; routing every exclusive or conditional write of a key to one ring owner makes that owner's per-path lock the cluster-wide serialization point without a distributed lock round trip. Outcomes of a transaction are replayed rather than re-run on a retried request_id, because a re-run could write a stale mutation over whatever superseded it. Read-only and other verdicts are returned in the response body with a code, since clients treat gRPC errors as transport failures and fail over.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.when: Every gateway write and lookup via S3ApiServer.withFilerClient; routed writes from s3api_object_routed_write.go and s3api_object_versioned_finalize.go; mounts and shell for the plain calls.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.ux: S3 clients get atomic If-Match / If-None-Match, consistent latest-version answers and WORM guards; mounts get ordered metadata.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go.if_broken: Conditional writes race and both succeed, versions or delete markers are lost, chunks still referenced by a live entry are deleted, or a retry applies a transaction twice.
gotchas: ObjectTransaction serializes but does not roll back: mutations apply one by one, and a failure at mutation i leaves mutations 0..i-1 applied (failed_mutation tells the caller which).

The request_id replay record lives in this filer's memory for 2 minutes and at most 10,000 unexpired entries; a filer restart, or a full table (the new record is then dropped), turns a retry into a re-application.

RECOMPUTE_LATEST with descending order lists the whole scanned directory under the object's lock on every call, since the store has no reverse listing; a key with many versions pays that on each versioned write and delete.
Plain (unconditional) creates and updates are not forwarded and run under the local filer's lock only.
UpdateEntry reports a failed condition as codes.FailedPrecondition and a missing entry as codes.NotFound, never in the response body; CreateEntry reports PRECONDITION_FAILED in the body.
DeleteEntry with expected_extended fails as FailedPrecondition when the entry is missing, even if every expected value asserts absence.
LookupDirectoryEntry returns the raw ErrNotFound, which crosses gRPC as codes.Unknown with its text; filer_pb.LookupEntry relies on that text.
AppendToEntry commits with context.Background(), so the caller's deadline and metadata event sink do not reach the store write.
AssignVolume returns a master assignment failure as text only, without an error_code; only the read-only verdict is coded.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..character: Evaluation of WriteCondition clauses against the current entry, with an ETag that mirrors the S3 gateway's
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..what: writeConditionSatisfied ANDs the clauses. IF_NOT_EXISTS / IF_EXISTS test presence, IF_OBJECT_EXISTS also refuses a plain directory that holds no object of its own (for If-Match: * on a null version, #12624); IF_ETAG_MATCH holds when the entry exists and its ETag is in the set, IF_ETAG_NOT_MATCH when it is absent or in none (RFC 7232 strong comparison unless allow_weak, which ignores W/ on both sides); IF_UNMODIFIED_SINCE / IF_MODIFIED_SINCE compare mtime in whole seconds and hold for an absent entry; IF_EXTENDED_NOT_EQUAL holds unless the key equals the blocking value; IF_EXTENDED_TIME_ELAPSED holds unless the stored unix-second deadline is still in the future (only when the optional gate key equals the gate value, which expresses governance bypass), and an unparseable deadline blocks; IF_CHUNKS_EQUAL compares chunk fids as multisets; IF_ENTRY_EQUAL compares serialized entries with chunks matched by fid. An unknown kind fails closed. storedEntryETag uses the stored S3 ETag attribute, then the remote ETag while the entry still holds the remote bytes, then Md5, then the chunk ETag (empty for an empty object).
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..why: Consequence: object-lock, conditional PUT/DELETE and the chunk-preserving read-modify-write all reduce to these comparisons; a guard that evaluated open would delete a locked object or resurrect deleted needles. Design: generic primitives keep S3 out of the filer; fail-closed defaults (unknown kind, malformed deadline) favour blocking a write over letting it through.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..when: Under the path lock in CreateEntry, UpdateEntry, ObjectTransaction and its per-mutation guards.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..ux: 412 PreconditionFailed and object-lock refusals that match AWS.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_condition..if_broken: Conditional writes pass that should fail (overwrites, deleted locked versions) or fail that should pass.
gotchas: storedEntryETag must stay in step with the gateway's ETag precedence; a divergence makes If-Match fail on objects whose ETag the client just read.
Retention deadlines are compared with the filer's clock.
IF_ENTRY_EQUAL with no expected entry holds only when the entry is absent.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.character: Route-by-key plumbing for the filer side: who owns a key's writes, forwarding to it, and verifying a forwarded hop
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.what: writeOwner asks the DLM lock ring for a key's write owner ('' when this filer owns it or there is no ring; a previous owner keeps the key through the cooling-off window of a ring change). forwardToWriteOwner sends the request to the owner and never re-sends it elsewhere on failure. entryRouteKey prefixes the path with the gateway's ObjectWriteRouteKeyPrefix so CreateEntry and an ObjectTransaction of the same object reach the same owner. checkMovedMarker accepts an is_moved request on a non-owner only when it arrived from a ring member's IP (movedFromPeer, with member hostnames resolved in parallel and cached for 5 minutes per membership), else answers PermissionDenied.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.why: Consequence: a forwarded request lost in transit and one the owner never saw look the same (Unavailable), so a retry on another filer could apply a committed write twice; an unreachable owner may also be partitioned rather than down. Design: fail the request and let the ring hand the key on after the cooling-off window, which bounds the outage. The is_moved marker is caller-controlled, so it is trusted only from ring members, to stop a client from forcing a conditional write under a non-owner's lock.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.when: Every forwarded CreateEntry, UpdateEntry, DeleteEntry and ObjectTransaction.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.ux: During an owner outage, writes to its keys fail until the ring moves on.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_route.go.if_broken: Two filers both apply a key's conditional writes (lost atomicity), or forwards loop between filers that disagree on the ring.
gotchas: movedFromPeer checks the peer IP only: any process on a ring member's host (for example an S3 gateway co-located with a filer) can send an accepted is_moved.
A failed DNS lookup of a member is not cached, so the next forwarded request resolves again.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.character: Cluster-facing informational RPCs of the filer: statistics, ping and its configuration
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.what: Statistics relays the master's capacity numbers (total, used, file count and their single-copy logical forms), asking with the filer's default replication when the caller names none, so free space is sized by the copies this filer's writes will make. Ping answers a self-probe for an empty target and otherwise only pings a peer the filer already knows: a filer the meta aggregator follows, a volume server the master client reports, or a configured or discovered master; it returns the start, remote and stop times. GetFilerConfiguration returns masters, default collection and replication, max chunk MB, the buckets directory, cipher flag, signature, metrics push settings, version and filer group.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.why: Consequence: an unrestricted Ping would make the filer an arbitrary outbound dialer for anyone who can reach its gRPC port. Design: target allow-list from state the filer already holds, all O(1) lookups. GetFilerConfiguration is how clients (the S3 gateway, mounts, shell) learn the buckets path, cipher mode and signature instead of being configured twice.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.when: S3 gateway startup (GetFilerConfiguration for DirBuckets, cipher and filer group), weed shell cluster.check and volume tools (Ping, Statistics), mounts.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.ux: Correct free-space numbers in df-style views; health checks that reach only cluster members.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_admin.go.if_broken: The gateway uses the wrong buckets path or cipher setting, capacity is misreported by a factor of the replica count, or Ping becomes an SSRF primitive.
gotchas: Ping to a master dials with context.Background(), so the caller's deadline bounds only the Ping RPC, not the connection setup.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_kv.go.character: The filer store's key-value side door over gRPC
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_kv.go.what: KvGet reads a raw key from the filer store (a missing key is an empty value, not an error); KvPut writes it, and an empty value deletes the key. Store errors come back in the response's error string.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_kv.go.why: Design: small cluster state that is not a file (sync offsets, checkpoints, tool state) lives in the same store as the metadata, so it is as durable and replicated as the store itself.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_kv.go.when: filer.sync / replication offsets, filer.remote.sync and other tools that persist a cursor.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_kv.go.if_broken: Sync tools lose their checkpoint and replay or skip changes.
gotchas: There is no way to store an empty value: KvPut with an empty value is a delete.
The RPCs carry no per-key authorization; access is whatever the filer's gRPC transport security allows.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.character: gRPC face of the mount peer registry used for peer-to-peer chunk sharing
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.what: MountRegister records or refreshes a mount's advertised peer address with its data center, rack and TTL; MountList returns the live entries with their last-seen times. runMountPeerRegistrySweeper evicts expired entries every 60 s (List also evicts lazily).
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.why: Consequence: mounts that read the same data can fetch chunks from each other instead of from volume servers, which needs a shared view of who is alive. Design: a soft-state registry with TTL heartbeats; each mount builds its rendezvous-hash view from MountList.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.when: weed mount with peer chunk sharing enabled: periodic register and list.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.ux: Lower volume-server load and faster repeated reads across mounts.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_mount_peer.if_broken: Mounts stop sharing chunks (more volume reads) or keep sending requests to departed peers.
gotchas: The advertised peer_addr and the TTL are taken from the request as given; the filer does not check them against the caller's address.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.character: Registry record and listing RPC for this filer's connected metadata subscribers
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.what: metadataSubscriber holds one connected subscriber (name '<type>@<address>', type, address, path prefix, client id and epoch, connect time), created on subscribe and removed on disconnect under knownListenersLock. ListMetadataSubscribers returns them, optionally filtered by client type, sorted by name then prefix, each tagged with this filer's address.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.why: Design: an admin view of who is following metadata (mounts, S3 gateways, filer.sync, peer filers) without scraping logs. Each filer knows only its own subscribers, so a cluster view queries every filer.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.when: The admin UI and shell tools listing subscribers.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.ux: Operators can see which mounts and gateways are connected.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_subscriber.if_broken: The admin page shows stale or missing subscribers.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.character: The batched exact-path lookup RPC: up to 4096 entries in one call, with their volume locations and read tokens
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.what: LookupDirectoryEntries validates the batch (1 to 4096 requests, absolute directories, a plain name without '/', '.', '..' or NUL), looks the paths up with up to 32 workers through fencedFindEntry (each result keeps its own log fence), keeping request order. A miss is found=false, a lookup error is an error on that item. It then collects the volume ids of every found entry's chunks and resolves them in one deduplicated master lookup: from the cache, or authoritatively when the caller set unavailable_volume_is_miss. A volume with no locations marks every entry that uses it with an error, except that for a cache caller an authoritative 'master does not serve it' turns the entry into a miss. When volume read guarding is on, each chunk fid gets a short-lived read JWT in read_auth.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.why: Consequence: clients that resolve many small objects (mount caches, gateways) paid one RPC per path and then one volume lookup per entry. Design: one bounded RPC and one location map; per-item fences so a cache can order each result against the metadata events it has seen. DeletedVids is a best-effort invalidation hint, so a cache that treats an unknown volume as a miss must confirm with the master rather than its own cache. Exact-fid tokens let a data-plane client read just these needles instead of holding a service credential for all of them.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.when: Mounts and other cache clients resolving many paths at once.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.ux: Faster cold reads of many small files.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_batch_look.if_broken: Caches serve entries whose volumes are gone, or misses that are really transient master failures.
gotchas: Locations and read tokens cover the entry's own chunks; for a manifest chunk that is the manifest needle's volume, not the volumes of the data chunks the manifest lists.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.character: The distributed lock manager's gRPC face: lock, unlock and owner lookup with one-hop forwarding, plus primary-to-backup replication and hand-off on ring changes
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.what: DistributedLock asks the local DLM to take or renew a named lock until now + seconds_to_lock; when the ring says another filer is the lock's host it forwards once (is_moved, checked with checkMovedMarker) and returns that filer's token, owner, generation and error, plus lock_host_moved_to. DistributedUnlock and FindLockOwner forward the same way; an unknown lock is NotFound. ReplicateLock applies a primary's insert or unlock on this backup, ordered by generation and seq. TransferLocks inserts locks handed over by another filer. OnDlmChangeSnapshot, run on every ring change, promotes backup locks this filer now owns and re-replicates them, transfers primary locks to their new primary before demoting them (keeping them if the transfer fails), and hands off locks it no longer holds any role for. SetupDlmReplication installs the replication callback (3 s timeout, failures only logged).
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.why: Consequence: the S3 gateway's object write lock, AppendToEntry and other cluster-wide mutual exclusion depend on a lock surviving the loss of the filer holding it. Design: each lock has a primary and a backup on the consistent-hash ring, replication is asynchronous with sequence numbers so stale mutations are rejected, and a primary demotes only after a successful hand-off.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.when: cluster.LockClient users: the S3 gateway's distributed object write lock (the fallback path when route-by-key is unavailable), AppendToEntry, shell and admin exclusive operations.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.ux: Concurrent writers to one key serialize; a filer restart does not drop held locks.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_dlm.go.if_broken: Two holders of the same lock (lost writes), or locks that never release and block writers until expiry.
gotchas: TransferLocks and ReplicateLock take no is_moved or peer check: any client that reaches the filer's gRPC port can insert a lock with any token and owner.
seconds_to_lock comes from the request without an upper bound.
Replication to the backup is fire-and-forget; a lock acquired just before its primary dies may not exist on the backup that is promoted.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.character: Advisory POSIX and flock locks for weed mount, held in the owner filer's memory with leases, warm-up and a cooling-window probe
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.what: PosixLock resolves the inode key's primary on the DLM ring and forwards to it once; the owner applies the operation to its in-memory table: TRY_LOCK (grant or report the conflict), UNLOCK, GET_LK, RELEASE_POSIX_OWNER (on flush), RELEASE_FLOCK_OWNER (on release) and KEEP_ALIVE (renew the mount session's lease, or re-assert its full set of held locks so a new owner can rebuild). A sweeper reaps sessions without a keepalive for 15 s. For 10 s after start, and while a ring change's previous owner may still hold locks (it is asked with a cooling_probe GET_LK under a 2 s deadline), a grant that cannot be confirmed safe is deferred: the client sees EAGAIN or retries, never a double grant.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.why: Consequence: applications on different mounts (databases, build tools) rely on fcntl/flock to exclude each other; a double grant corrupts their files. Design: one authority per inode (the ring owner) with soft state rebuilt from client re-assertions after restart or ownership change, preferring a deferred grant over an unsafe one. Blocking waits (SetLkw) are polled by the mount, so the filer never parks an RPC.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.when: weed mount with -posixLock: every fcntl/flock call and the session keepalive.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.ux: Cross-mount advisory locking that behaves like a local filesystem's, with brief EAGAINs around filer restarts.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_posix_lock.if_broken: Two mounts both hold a write lock on the same range, or locks of a dead mount are never released.
gotchas: Lock state is memory only; correctness after a restart depends on every mount re-asserting its locks within the warm-up window.
The owner is the ring primary (GetPrimary), not writeOwner's choice that keeps the previous owner through the cooling window; the cooling probe covers that gap instead.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.character: The server side of TraverseBfsMetadata: stream every entry under a directory, as a breadth-first walk or from one store snapshot
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.what: TraverseBfsMetadata finds the start directory, skips paths under excluded prefixes (matched on a path-component boundary through a ptrie), and by default sends the start entry and then walks breadth first, listing 1024 entries per page (iterateDirectory) and queuing only directory paths; each response carries the path's commit timestamp (EntryCommitTsNs, falling back to mtime). When the request metadata asks for snapshot mode and the store implements filer.EntryScanner, it streams the store's snapshot scan instead (any order, entry_ts_ns 0) and says so in the response header; a store that declines before yielding anything falls back to the walk.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.why: Consequence: a peer filer bootstrapping or an fs.meta.save export reads a whole tree, and holding queued entries with their chunk lists exhausted the filer's memory on large trees. Design: queue paths, stream entries. Snapshot mode gives a consistent image where the store can provide one; the walk gives the per-path timestamps consumers that replay events need.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.when: filer.go peer bootstrap (StreamBfs from the meta aggregator, excluding the system log directory), weed shell fs.meta.save, the admin file browser's metadata export.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.ux: Metadata exports and new-filer bootstrap complete on large namespaces.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_traverse_m.if_broken: Bootstraps run the filer out of memory, or exports leak excluded subtrees (the admin export excludes /etc for read-only roles).
gotchas: An excluded prefix with a trailing slash excludes nothing below it: the component-boundary check needs the character after the prefix to be '/'. Callers pass prefixes without one.
The walk is not a snapshot: entries changed during it may appear in their old or new form.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.character: The StreamMutateEntry bidirectional stream: one ordered pipe for a mount's creates, updates, deletes and renames
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.what: StreamMutateEntry receives requests in a loop and runs each in its own goroutine (at most 1024 outstanding per stream) after admission by the per-stream mutateScheduler (64 concurrent, path-ordered). Each request is handled by the ordinary CreateEntry, UpdateEntry, DeleteEntry or StreamRenameEntry and answered with its request_id; renames go through renameStreamProxy, which forwards each rename event as a non-final message and then a final is_last message. Sends are serialized by syncStream's mutex. A failed operation carries its error text and an errno; an unknown request type answers EINVAL so the client's waiter is released. The first failed Send ends the stream after in-flight work drains.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.why: Consequence: a FUSE mount issues many small metadata mutations; one RPC each cost a round trip and gave no ordering between them. Design: one stream per mount keeps arrival order per path while letting unrelated paths run in parallel, and the receive loop blocks only on the outstanding cap, so a conflicted path cannot stall receipt of unrelated ones.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.ux: Faster file creation and rename in mounts, with POSIX-ordered results.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.if_broken: Mount operations are applied out of order (a rename before the create it depends on) or hang waiting for a response that never comes.
gotchas: Every create, update and delete failure is reported as EIO, whatever the cause (a missing entry, an existing name, a failed precondition); only renames map 'not found', 'not empty' and 'not directory' text to ENOENT, ENOTEMPTY and ENOTDIR.
The proxy's RecvMsg fails on purpose: a rename must never read from the shared stream.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.character: Path-keyed admission control for StreamMutateEntry, with subtree barriers, ported from filer.sync's MetadataProcessor
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.what: classifyMutation gives each request its path(s) and kind: a file event, a barrier directory event (directory create, every delete, every rename with both old and new paths) or a non-barrier directory attribute update; malformed requests become a barrier at '/'. Admit queues the waiter on each of its paths and admits it only when it heads every queue it joined, conflicts with nothing active (a barrier blocks its path and every descendant; a file conflicts with a file at the same path; a barrier waits for active descendants to drain) and the 64-slot limit allows. Done releases the slot and promotes newly admissible heads.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.why: Consequence: two requests for the same path on one stream must apply in arrival order, and a directory rename must not interleave with writes inside it. Design: per-path FIFO queues on top of the conflict rules, so even a condition broadcast cannot reorder same-path requests; attribute-only directory updates do not serialize their subtree.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.when: Every request on a StreamMutateEntry stream.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.ux: None directly; it is why mount operations on one stream appear in order.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_stream_mut.if_broken: Out-of-order mutations, or a stream that deadlocks when a waiter is never promoted.
gotchas: Ordering is per stream only; two mounts writing the same path are serialized by the filer's path lock, not by this scheduler.
Every delete is a barrier because the request does not say whether it targets a directory, so a delete waits for all active work under its path.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.character: Rename of a file or a whole directory tree inside one store transaction, with deferred chunk and remote-object cleanup
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.what: AtomicRenameEntry and StreamRenameEntry check CanRename, lock the old and new paths (in path order, descendants unlocked), open a store transaction, and call moveEntry. moveSelfEntry refuses a file over a directory and the reverse, deletes an existing target (events suppressed), inserts the new entry with the same attributes, chunks, extended attributes and hard-link data, then for a directory moves every child recursively 1024 at a time (moveFolderSubEntries) and deletes the old entry. Chunks of an overwritten target are deleted only after the commit; metadata events are queued and published after the commit. Remote-only entries are copied on the remote first, or, over a remote-only target, after the commit with the new entry reading the old key (ExtRemoteRenameSourceKey) until the copy lands; old remote objects are deleted after the commit only when no remote-only entry has taken their path. AtomicRenameEntry can refuse an existing target (fail_if_target_exists, under the path locks). StreamRenameEntry follows POSIX for directories: the target must be an empty directory; it streams each child's move event to the caller.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.why: Consequence: a rename that failed halfway and had already deleted the target's chunks would leave live metadata pointing at freed needles. Design: everything destructive (chunk deletes, remote deletes, events) waits for the commit, and a failed rename releases its commit stamps so the delivered and flushed watermarks are not pinned below it. Path locks are held through notification so a fenced lookup never sees renamed state under an earlier fence.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.when: S3 object rename extensions and s3tables moves (AtomicRenameEntry), mounts (StreamRenameEntry, also via StreamMutateEntry), shell mv.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.ux: mv in a mount and rename APIs behave atomically on transactional stores.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.if_broken: Renamed trees lose children, overwritten targets leave orphaned or prematurely freed chunks, or remote-mounted objects are deleted while still referenced.
gotchas: On stores without transactions (BeginTransaction is a no-op: the LevelDB and most KV stores), a directory rename that fails midway leaves some children moved and some not.
A directory rename copies and deletes every descendant entry: its cost is proportional to the subtree size, and descendants are not locked while it runs.
StreamRenameEntry sends each move event to the caller before the commit, so a client can see events for a rename that is then rolled back.
AtomicRenameEntry has no empty-target-directory check; moving a directory over a non-empty one fails only because the target delete is not recursive.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_rename.go.issue_note: StreamRenameEntry leaks the store transaction when a directory is renamed onto a non-empty directory. It calls BeginTransaction, then for a directory source checks the target and, on 'is not empty', returns the error without RollbackTransaction (filer_grpc_server_rename.go, the ListDirectoryEntries check after FindEntry(targetDir)); the 'is not directory' branch just above does roll back. On the SQL stores BeginTransaction opens a *sql.Tx with BeginTx on a context the wrapper has detached from cancellation (filerstore_wrapper.go: context.WithoutCancel), so database/sql never rolls it back: each such rename holds one pooled connection until the filer restarts. A mount where users repeatedly 'mv dir existing-nonempty-dir' (or a tool retrying it) drains the pool, after which every store call waits for a connection. The emptiness check also lists with context.Background() rather than the transaction context, so on SQL stores it reads outside the transaction. Found by reading at 917cf534; not reproduced. The fix is a RollbackTransaction before that return.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.character: CacheRemoteObjectToLocalCluster: pull a remote-mounted object into local volume needles and point its entry at them
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.what: The handler rejects an entry larger than the caller's max_size before joining a singleflight per path, runs the download on a context detached from the caller (a caller that leaves gets ctx.Err() while the download continues), and retries with its own flight when a shared flight failed only on a co-caller's tighter size bound. doCacheRemoteObjectToLocalCluster returns the entry as is when it is not remote-only or already has chunks; otherwise it resolves the mount mapping and remote conf freshly from /etc/remote, picks a chunk size aiming at about 32 chunks (5 MiB floor, the filer's max MB cap, at most 1000 chunks), and for each chunk assigns a needle and asks the volume server to FetchAndWriteNeedle the byte range straight from the remote (8 chunks in parallel by default, capped at 1024; per-chunk multipart download concurrency passed through). On failure it deletes the needles already written, triggers remote-cache eviction on capacity errors, and, when the remote confirms the object is gone, prunes the entry with a conditional ObjectTransaction (IF_ENTRY_EQUAL, keep remote) unless it is a version file, hard link, inline-content entry or under an active object lock. On success it re-reads the entry under the path lock, discards the download if the entry changed meanwhile, else stores the chunks with last_local_sync_ts_ns and publishes an update event.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.why: Consequence: reading a remote-mounted object through the gateway needs its bytes local, and many readers of one cold object would otherwise each start a download. Design: the volume servers fetch directly from the remote, so data never passes through the filer; the detached context keeps a long download from being thrown away (and its needles deleted) every time an impatient caller times out. Not-found sentinels are re-coded as codes.NotFound because a raw error crosses gRPC as Unknown.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.when: The S3 gateway when GetObject or CopyObject hits a remote-only entry (s3api cacheRemoteObjectForCopy and the read path), the filer HTTP read path, weed shell remote.cache.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.ux: The first read of a remote-mounted object is slow or answered 503 + Retry-After by the gateway; later reads are local.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_remote.go.if_broken: Cold objects never become readable, downloads leak needles on every retry, or a concurrent overwrite is clobbered by a stale cached copy.
gotchas: The commit takes this filer's path lock, not the key's ring owner's, and writes with Store.UpdateEntry directly.
After the first failed chunk the other workers keep downloading; their needles are deleted only once all finish.

weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.character: Metadata subscription streams: replay a filer's persisted metadata log and then follow its in-memory log, for one filer or aggregated across peers, with gap detection and watermark holds
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.what: SubscribeMetadata serves the aggregated stream (this filer's events merged with every peer's, through the MetaAggregator's log buffer) once peers exist; a single filer, or one whose peers have not appeared yet, serves the local stream and ends it with errAggregationUpgrade when a peer arrives so the client reconnects for the aggregated one. SubscribeLocalMetadata serves only this filer's events. Each stream registers the client (client_id and epoch: a newer epoch replaces, a duplicate is refused), then loops: read the persisted log from disk from the cursor (or, for clients that read volume chunks themselves, send LogFileChunkRefs in batches of 64 and only the chunks not sent before), then follow the in-memory buffer until it is exhausted, and repeat. Events pass the path filter twice: a cheap skeleton scan before unmarshaling (filer_pb_event_scan.go) and the full match after; events from the subscriber's own signature are dropped, the filer's signature is appended, the system log directory is never sent, and after 1000 filtered events an empty event carries the timestamp forward. pipelinedSender decouples reading from gRPC sends (1024 buffered) and, for clients that support batching, packs up to 256 events per Send when they are more than 2 minutes behind. Idle heartbeats (5 s, or a 200 ms delivery claim on a filer with peers) and flush reports tell caught-up clients how far delivery and flushing have reached. When the in-memory buffer has evicted the range after the cursor and the disk does not hold it yet, the subscriber parks (gapStallReporter, metrics) and gives up after 15 minutes, skipping the gap with an error log. The aggregated stream also holds reads at the peers' low delivery and flush watermarks so an event from a slower peer cannot be skipped past, with a settled-horizon escape when a peer's watermark stalls.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.why: Consequence: S3 gateways (IAM, bucket config and circuit-breaker caches), mounts, filer.sync, backup and replication all learn about changes only through this stream; a skipped event is a stale cache or an unreplicated file, a duplicated one is usually harmless. Design: a subscriber resumes from a timestamp, so the server must prove a range is either on disk or still in memory before moving the cursor past it, and with several filers it must not deliver beyond the slowest peer's watermark. Giving up after a bounded stall trades completeness for liveness when a peer is dead, and the skip is counted and logged.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.when: Long-lived streams from every metadata follower; the S3 gateway subscribes to /etc/ at startup (s3api_server.go subscribeMetaEvents).
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.ux: Changes made through one gateway or filer show up in the others' caches within moments; a stalled peer delays them by up to its watermark horizon.
weed/server/filer_grpc_server_sub_meta.g.if_broken: Caches and replicas silently miss changes (stale IAM credentials, bucket policies, circuit-breaker limits), or followers spin re-reading the same log files.
gotchas: A subscriber with client_id 0 is never registered, and hasClient answers false for it, so the loop ends such a stream at its first liveness check; followers must send a non-zero id.
After 15 minutes parked on an unprovable gap the stream skips the range: events a peer flushes into it later are never delivered to that subscriber.
The local stream negates client_id (req.ClientId = -req.ClientId) so a client's local and aggregated subscriptions do not collide in the registry.
Filtering is by path only; a subscriber that wants a narrow set of events still costs the filer a skeleton scan of every logged event.

weed/filer/filer.go.character: The Filer core: construction and peer bootstrap, the entry create / update / find paths with parent-directory creation and lazy TTL expiry, and the empty-parent cleanup
weed/filer/filer.go.what: NewFiler wires the master client, deletion queue and its durable ledger, filer conf, remote storage, the DLM, the persisted-log cache, remote-deletion tombstones, the entry lock table and the local metadata log buffer (flushed every minute; metadata-log chunks optionally sent to their own collection). MaybeBootstrapFromOnePeer copies the oldest peer's whole tree through StreamBfs; AggregateFromPeers sets the DLM ring (thereafter fed by the master's LockRingUpdates), creates the empty-folder cleaner on the same ring and the MetaAggregator, subscribing to itself first and then to each peer. ListExistingPeerUpdates prefers the leader's list, polling it briefly when empty. SetStore wraps the store and loads or creates the store signature. CreateEntry refuses '/', over-long names and dot segments, clears directory TTLs, then either inserts a new entry (stable inode, commit stamp) and creates missing parents afterwards (ensureParentDirectoryEntry: validates a bucket name under /buckets, promotes a file in the way to a prefix-object directory keeping its data), or, unless O_EXCL, updates the existing one (a prefix object landing on a directory keeps the directory's mode, owner and xattr- keys); it then publishes the event and deletes chunks the new entry no longer uses. UpdateEntry keeps crtime and inode, refuses a file/directory type change with sentinels, and clears a remote entry's sync stamp when local content changed. FindEntry serves '/' from a constant, expires TTL'd files on read, and falls back to a lazy remote fetch. doListDirectoryEntries expires TTL'd files while listing (after the listing, to avoid store deadlocks), then may remove now-empty parents (DeleteEmptyParentDirectories, never at or above bucket level). EnsureDirectoryEntry and DirectoryAttributes let the empty-folder cleaner restore a directory it removed without widening its mode. Shutdown drains the log buffer, the aggregator and the deletion ledger before closing the store.
weed/filer/filer.go.why: Consequence: every S3 object, version file, bucket and mount file is an entry written through CreateEntry, so its parent creation, prefix-object promotion and chunk cleanup decide whether nested keys coexist and whether data is freed correctly. Design: the entry is inserted before its parents, because a parent checked first can be removed by the empty-folder cleaner before the entry lands and nothing would look again; a failed parent creation leaves the entry in place unannounced rather than delete by path what a concurrent create may own. TTL expiry is lazy, on read and list, so no sweeper has to scan the namespace.
weed/filer/filer.go.when: Every metadata mutation and lookup on the filer; startup and peer membership changes.
weed/filer/filer.go.ux: S3 keys like a and a/b can both exist; expired objects disappear on access; empty folders under buckets vanish when their last expiring file goes.
weed/filer/filer.go.if_broken: Nested keys overwrite or hide each other, parents are missing, chunks are freed under live entries, or expired data lingers.
gotchas: Expiry on read or list deletes from the store without a metadata event for plain-TTL entries (Store.DeleteOneEntry): peers and subscribers such as mount caches only learn when they expire it themselves.

DeleteEmptyParentDirectories removes directories through doDeleteEntryMetaAndData, which publishes events only for files, so those directory deletes are never announced either; it also ignores a bucket's allow-empty-folders setting.
ensureParentDirectoryEntry validates bucket names only when the second path component is literally 'buckets', not DirBucketsPath, and checks the lenient VerifyS3BucketName.
A read through FindEntry can delete an entry (expiry), including under the shared lock fencedFindEntry holds.
CreateEntry on '/' is a silent no-op.

weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.character: Entry and subtree deletion: children first, remote objects and tombstones, chunk and hard-link cleanup, and bucket collection drops
weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.what: DeleteEntryMetaAndData finds the entry (honouring an if-not-modified-after cutoff), and for a directory deletes its children first (doBatchDeleteFolderMetaAndData: lists 1024 at a time, refuses a non-recursive delete of a non-empty folder with ErrNonEmptyFolder, recurses into subdirectories, deletes each file's remote object unless the delete is metadata-only, publishes a delete event per file, collects chunks, then sweeps the store with DeleteFolderChildren and publishes the directory's event). Deleting a bucket may skip the listing when the store can drop a whole bucket, and drops the bucket's collection through the master when nothing else can route into it (bucketCollection checks the filer group name, storage rules, the metadata-log collections and sibling buckets), within 15 s that outlive the caller. Chunks are deleted after the metadata, except for a hard link with other links left. Recursive deletes tombstone the directory and each child for remote lazy reads before deleting. WithKeepRemoteObject makes a delete metadata-only (marked in the event so remote sync daemons leave the object too); deleting an empty folder under a remote mount is made metadata-only automatically, since its remote prefix may still hold unread objects. DeleteEntryError and IsNonEmptyFolderError restore the non-empty sentinel from response text.
weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.why: Consequence: S3 DeleteObject, DeleteBucket, lifecycle and mount rm all end here; deleting chunks before metadata would leave entries pointing at freed needles, and dropping a collection another path still writes to destroys that data. Design: metadata first, chunks after; collection drop only when provably exclusive, with listing failures keeping it.
weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.when: DeleteEntry RPC and HTTP deletes, ObjectTransaction DELETE mutations, rename target replacement, bucket deletion.
weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.ux: Deleting a bucket frees its volumes quickly when it owns its collection; rm -r in mounts works on large trees.
weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go.if_broken: Deleted objects' data is never reclaimed, data is reclaimed while still referenced, or a bucket delete removes volumes shared with other buckets.
gotchas: doDeleteEntryMetaAndData publishes no event for a directory; only doBatchDeleteFolderMetaAndData does. A caller that deletes a directory through it alone (DeleteEmptyParentDirectories, the lazy remote path) leaves subscribers unaware.
With ignoreRecursiveError a failed remote delete is logged and the walk continues, so metadata can be gone while the remote object remains.
The non-empty check looks only at the first page of the first listing; children that race in afterwards are not swept by a non-recursive delete.

weed/filer/filer_rename.go.character: Rename preconditions shared by both rename RPCs
weed/filer/filer_rename.go.what: CanRename refuses moving a directory into itself or a descendant, renaming a bucket directory, and any move whose source and target lie in different buckets (or between a bucket and a non-bucket path). DetectBucket returns the bucket a path is under, or ''.
weed/filer/filer_rename.go.why: Consequence: each bucket maps to its own collection, so a cross-bucket rename would leave an entry in one bucket pointing at chunks in another bucket's collection, which a later bucket delete would drop. Design: refuse rather than copy data.
weed/filer/filer_rename.go.when: AtomicRenameEntry and StreamRenameEntry, before taking locks.
weed/filer/filer_rename.go.ux: mv across buckets in a mount fails; S3 has no cross-bucket rename anyway.
weed/filer/filer_rename.go.if_broken: Objects whose chunks vanish when another bucket is deleted, or a bucket renamed out from under its collection.
gotchas: The checks run before the rename takes its path locks; the entry can change between CanRename and the move.

weed/filer/filer_search.go.character: Directory listing with a name prefix, glob include/exclude patterns and expired-entry skipping
weed/filer/filer_search.go.what: ListDirectoryEntries reads limit+1 entries to report hasMore; CountDirectoryEntries counts up to a limit. StreamListDirectoryEntries trims a trailing slash, turns the literal head of a glob into a store prefix, and re-lists to make up for entries filtered out by the pattern (filepath.Match on the rest) or the exclude pattern, and doListValidEntries re-lists to make up for expired entries skipped, so a caller still gets up to limit live, matching entries.
weed/filer/filer_search.go.why: Design: stores only list by name prefix, so pattern filtering happens here, and the make-up loops keep the page size honest without the store knowing about TTLs or globs.
weed/filer/filer_search.go.when: Every directory listing: the ListEntries RPC, the filer HTTP directory view (?namePattern=, ?namePatternExclude=), renames and deletes walking a tree.
weed/filer/filer_search.go.ux: Filer UI and API listings with patterns.
weed/filer/filer_search.go.if_broken: Short pages that clients take for the end of a directory, or listings that loop.
gotchas: A namePattern without '*' or '?' is ignored: splitPattern returns an empty prefix and an empty rest, so the listing is unfiltered.
A prefix and a namePattern are documented as mutually exclusive; a pattern's literal head replaces the prefix.

weed/filer/read_write.go.character: Helpers that read and write small files kept inside the filer, through a filer client
weed/filer/read_write.go.what: ReadEntry looks an entry up and writes its inline content, or streams its chunks from volume servers, into a buffer. ReadInsideFiler returns an entry's inline content only. SaveInsideFiler creates the entry with inline content, or updates it, stamping size, mtime and the content MD5 on every write, and skips the write when content and MD5 already match.
weed/filer/read_write.go.why: Consequence: configuration lives in small filer files (/etc/iam, /etc/s3, filer.conf, circuit breaker, remote mounts), read and written by many components. Design: the MD5 is restamped on every write so the entry's ETag describes what is stored, since conditional writers key IF_ETAG_MATCH off it.
weed/filer/read_write.go.when: The S3 gateway's config loads (ReadInsideFiler for IAM, circuit breaker, bucket policies), shell commands saving configs, filer conf loading.
weed/filer/read_write.go.if_broken: Config changes do not persist, or a conditional writer accepts a stale ETag and overwrites a newer config.
gotchas: SaveInsideFiler is a lookup then an unconditional create or update: two concurrent writers race and the last write wins.
ReadInsideFiler returns only inline content; an entry whose content was written as chunks reads as empty.

weed/filer/zip_extract.go.character: Safety limits for extracting a zip archive uploaded to the filer
weed/filer/zip_extract.go.what: SpoolZipReader buffers an uploaded archive for random access: in memory up to 32 MiB, else in a temp file, never more than the caller's limit (default 5 GiB), failing with ErrZipTooLarge one byte past it. CheckZipLimits caps members at 100,000 and the declared uncompressed total at 1 TiB. SanitizeZipMemberName maps a member to a relative filer path, refusing symlinks, devices, pipes, sockets, absolute paths, empty, '.', '..' or NUL segments and anything filepath.IsLocal rejects.
weed/filer/zip_extract.go.why: Consequence: an uploaded archive is attacker-controlled; without these limits it could fill the filer's disk, fan out to millions of entries or write outside the target directory. Design: errors are typed so handlers answer 4xx for oversized input.
weed/filer/zip_extract.go.when: The filer HTTP extract path (POST/PUT with extraction requested, filer_server_handlers_extract.go), including the S3 gateway's zip-extract upload.
weed/filer/zip_extract.go.ux: Uploading a zip with extraction creates its files under the target directory.
weed/filer/zip_extract.go.if_broken: Path traversal out of the target directory, or disk and memory exhaustion from one upload.
gotchas: The 1 TiB cap is checked against sizes the archive declares; actual expansion is bounded by archive/zip's own size checks while reading.

weed/filer/copy_params.go.character: Names of the query parameters and headers of the filer's server-side copy endpoint
weed/filer/copy_params.go.what: Constants for the copy request (cp.from, overwrite, dataOnly, a request id, and the expected source and destination inode, mtime and size) and the response headers that confirm the copy committed and echo its request id.
weed/filer/copy_params.go.why: Design: one definition shared by the filer handler and its client so the names cannot drift; the expected-attribute parameters let the client make the copy conditional on both files being what it last saw.
weed/filer/copy_params.go.when: weed mount's copy_file_range (weedfs_file_copy_range.go) and the filer's copy handler (filer_server_handlers_copy.go).
weed/filer/copy_params.go.ux: Server-side copies in mounts (cp --reflink-style copy_file_range) avoid moving data through the client.
weed/filer/copy_params.go.if_broken: Copies fail or overwrite a file that changed since the client looked.

weed/filer/filer_buckets.go.character: The one test for whether an entry is an S3 bucket directory
weed/filer/filer_buckets.go.what: IsBucket is true for a directory directly under DirBucketsPath whose name does not start with '.'.
weed/filer/filer_buckets.go.why: Design: buckets are just top-level directories under the buckets path; dot-names there (.system and similar) are internal.
weed/filer/filer_buckets.go.when: Deletes (collection drop, metrics cleanup), CanRename, bucket listing.
weed/filer/filer_buckets.go.if_broken: Deleting a bucket keeps its collection, or deleting an internal directory drops a collection.

weed/filer/filer_hardlink.go.what: NewHardLinkId returns 16 random bytes followed by the marker byte 0x01; HardLinkId is that 17-byte value.
weed/filer/filer_hardlink.go.why: Design: entries that are links share one id, under which the store keeps the shared inode record; the marker distinguishes these keys in the store's key space.
weed/filer/filer_hardlink.go.when: Mounts creating hard links; the store's hard-link indirection (filerstore_hardlink.go).
weed/filer/filer_hardlink.go.if_broken: Links stop sharing data, or link records collide with other KV keys.

weed/filer/filer_inode.go.character: Stable inode assignment for new entries
weed/filer/filer_inode.go.what: ensureEntryInode leaves a set inode alone; otherwise it fills a missing crtime and derives the inode the way weed mount does: from the hard-link id for links (so all links share one inode), else from the path and creation time.
weed/filer/filer_inode.go.why: Consequence: the mount and the filer must agree on inode numbers without a reverse index. Design: derive rather than allocate.
weed/filer/filer_inode.go.when: CreateEntry and parent-directory creation for every new entry; UpdateEntry when an old entry had none.
weed/filer/filer_inode.go.if_broken: Inodes change under applications, or hard links report different inodes.
gotchas: Two entries created at the same path within the same second get the same inode.

weed/filer/entry.go.character: The filer's in-memory Entry type and its conversions to and from filer_pb.Entry, plus the S3-lifecycle expiry marks
weed/filer/entry.go.what: Entry is a full path with Attr (mtime, crtime, ctime, atime, mode, uid/gid, mime, TTL, user and group names, symlink target, md5, file size, rdev, inode), the extended map, chunks, hard-link id and counter, inline content, remote entry, quota, WORM enforcement time and the commit timestamp of the mutation that produced it. Size is the largest of the chunk extent, the stored file size and the content length. ShallowClone copies the struct; ToProtoEntry / FromPbEntry convert, filling FileSize from the chunks. ApplyStorageTtl stamps the storage rule's TTL (never on remote entries) and, for S3 objects that are not versioned, marks SeaweedFSExpiresS3 so expiry counts from mtime rather than crtime; GetS3ExpireTime computes it.
weed/filer/entry.go.why: Consequence: every layer between the RPCs and the stores passes this type, so a field missing from a conversion is silently dropped on the next write. Design: S3 lifecycle TTLs must restart on overwrite (mtime), while plain filer TTLs count from creation; versioned entries are excluded because the S3 expiry path skips them, and stamping one would drop its expiry entirely.
weed/filer/entry.go.ux: S3 objects with a lifecycle TTL expire relative to their last write.
weed/filer/entry.go.if_broken: Fields lost between store and wire (quota, WORM time, commit stamps), or objects expiring from the wrong time.
gotchas: ShallowClone shares the Extended map and the Chunks slice with the original; callers that change either must clone them first, as the RPC handlers do.

weed/filer/entry_codec.go.character: Store encoding of an entry, attribute conversion, and the entry-equality test
weed/filer/entry_codec.go.what: EncodeAttributesAndChunks and DecodeAttributesAndChunks marshal an entry through pooled filer_pb.Entry messages (the encoded bytes are copied out before the message goes back to the pool). EntryAttributeToPb, EntryAttributeToExistingPb and PbToEntryAttribute convert attributes, keeping nanoseconds for mtime, ctime and atime (a missing ctime or atime decodes as mtime). EqualEntry compares attributes, chunks, extended attributes, md5, hard-link data, content, remote entry and quota.
weed/filer/entry_codec.go.why: Design: every store saves the same protobuf blob under its own key scheme, so the codec is shared; pooling cuts allocations on hot listing paths.
weed/filer/entry_codec.go.when: Every store read and write; EqualEntry in UpdateEntry (to skip no-op updates) and in the remote-cache commit.
weed/filer/entry_codec.go.if_broken: Entries that fail to decode, or no-op updates that are written and announced anyway (or real updates that are skipped).
gotchas: EqualEntry ignores WORMEnforcedAtTsNs and CommitTsNs, so an UpdateEntry RPC that changes only the WORM enforcement time is treated as no change and not written.
Crtime is stored in whole seconds; its nanoseconds are lost on every round trip.

weed/filer/entry_codec_attributes.go.character: Attributes-only decoding of a stored entry for listings that do not need chunks
weed/filer/entry_codec_attributes.go.what: DecodeListedEntry decodes in full, or, when the context asks for chunks to be omitted, DecodeAttributesOnly: it walks the protobuf fields, skips every chunks field while still computing the largest chunk end (offset + size) and validating the skipped chunk's nested messages and UTF-8 strings, unmarshals the rest, and raises FileSize to the chunk extent.
weed/filer/entry_codec_attributes.go.why: Consequence: decoding large chunk lists dominated mount readdir cost. Design: skip them but keep the size right for stores whose blobs never had FileSize folded in, and still reject a malformed blob that a full decode would reject.
weed/filer/entry_codec_attributes.go.when: Stores' listing paths when filer_pb.WithChunksOmitted is set (mount readdir).
weed/filer/entry_codec_attributes.go.if_broken: Listed files show size 0 or a corrupt entry slips through a listing.

weed/filer/configuration.go.what: LoadConfiguration requires exactly one enabled default store among the registered Stores (exits listing the supported ones if none, fatal if two), initializes a fresh instance and sets it, then initializes each '<store>.<id>.enabled' section as a path-specific store mounted at its required location.
weed/filer/configuration.go.why: Design: one default store plus optional per-path stores lets a subtree (for example a hot bucket) live in a different database.
weed/filer/configuration.go.ux: Operators choose LevelDB, SQL, Redis, Cassandra and others in filer.toml.
weed/filer/configuration.go.if_broken: The filer does not start, or a path's metadata lands in the wrong store.
gotchas: Path-specific stores are outside the default store's transactions (FilerStoreWrapper begins transactions on the default store only), so a rename across the boundary is not atomic.

weed/filer/filer_conf.go.character: Path-prefix storage rules (filer.conf): load, match, merge and edit
weed/filer/filer_conf.go.what: FilerConf keeps PathConf rules in a ptrie keyed by location prefix, loaded from /etc/seaweedfs/filer.conf (inline content or chunks; versions before 2 drop explicit false fsync and worm flags so they inherit). MatchStorageRule merges every rule whose prefix matches the path, outer to inner: strings and counts are overridden by the inner rule, read_only and disable_chunk_deletion are ORed, fsync and worm are tri-state. ApplyBucketQuotaReadOnly flips a bucket's read-only flag around its quota; ClearBucketReadOnly rewrites filer.conf with SaveInsideFiler; ClearBucketLifecycleDayTTLs drops legacy day-TTL rules a lifecycle once created (or clears the TTL on an operator's rule) and saves conditionally (If-Match on the content MD5, else if-unmodified-since). Also directory constants (/etc/, /etc/seaweedfs, /etc/remote, /etc/iam).
weed/filer/filer_conf.go.why: Consequence: these rules choose collection, replication, TTL, disk type, fsync, placement, read-only and WORM for every write, and the S3 gateway's bucket quota enforcement works by toggling read-only here. Design: prefix rules compose, so a bucket-level rule refines a cluster-wide one.
weed/filer/filer_conf.go.when: Every write's storage option (detectStorageOption), the S3 gateway's quota and lifecycle code, weed shell fs.configure.
weed/filer/filer_conf.go.ux: Per-bucket collections, TTLs, replication and quotas.
weed/filer/filer_conf.go.if_broken: Data lands in the wrong collection or replication, quotas never block writes, or a bucket stays read-only after it drops below quota.
gotchas: Matching is a plain string prefix: a rule for /buckets/a without a trailing slash also applies to /buckets/ab.
read_only is ORed down the chain, so an inner rule cannot make a path writable under a read-only outer rule.
doLoadConf stops at the first rule SetLocationConf rejects and returns nil, silently ignoring the rest.
ClearBucketReadOnly writes back with the unconditional SaveInsideFiler, while ClearBucketLifecycleDayTTLs uses a conditional write; a concurrent fs.configure edit can be lost to the former.

weed/filer/filerstore.go.character: The FilerStore interface every metadata backend implements, and its optional capabilities
weed/filer/filerstore.go.what: FilerStore: insert, update, find, delete, delete folder children, list (with and without a name prefix), transactions, KV get/put/delete, shutdown. Optional interfaces: EntryScanner (one consistent snapshot of a subtree), BucketAware (per-bucket tables: creation and deletion hooks, dropping a whole bucket), Debuggable. Sentinels for unsupported prefix listing, unsupported scans, unimplemented KV and KV misses.
weed/filer/filerstore.go.why: Design: a minimal interface lets many databases back the namespace; capabilities are discovered by type assertion so a store opts into what it can do well.
weed/filer/filerstore.go.when: Implemented by every store under weed/filer/*; called only through FilerStoreWrapper.
weed/filer/filerstore.go.if_broken: A store that half-implements a contract (for example a prefix listing that ignores the prefix) breaks S3 listings.
gotchas: A store that answers ErrUnsupportedListDirectoryPrefixed is served by the wrapper's client-side prefix filter, which scans the directory from the start name.

weed/filer/filerstore_hardlink.go.character: Hard-link indirection: the shared inode record kept in the store's KV under the hard-link id
weed/filer/filerstore_hardlink.go.what: On insert and update of a file with a hard-link id, the wrapper writes the entry's attributes and chunks into KV under that id (setHardLink) and, if the path previously held a different link, decrements the old one. maybeReadHardLink replaces a listed or found entry's attributes and chunks with the shared record. DeleteHardLink decrements the record's counter and deletes it at zero.
weed/filer/filerstore_hardlink.go.why: Consequence: all names of a hard link must see one file. Design: the per-path entry holds only the id; the data lives once in KV.
weed/filer/filerstore_hardlink.go.when: Every store operation on an entry with a hard-link id (mounts).
weed/filer/filerstore_hardlink.go.if_broken: Links diverge, or chunks are freed while another link still points at them.
gotchas: The counter decrement is an unlocked read-modify-write on KV; two concurrent unlinks of the same file can both read the same count, leaving the record (and its chunks) behind or deleting it early.

weed/filer/filerstore_translate_path.go.character: Adapter that makes a path-specific store see paths relative to its mount point
weed/filer/filerstore_translate_path.go.what: FilerStorePathTranslator strips the store's root from every path before calling the inner store and restores the full path on returned entries, for every FilerStore method; KV calls pass through.
weed/filer/filerstore_translate_path.go.why: Design: a path-specific store can be the same implementation as the default store and need not know where it is mounted.
weed/filer/filerstore_translate_path.go.when: Wraps each store added by AddPathSpecificStore.
weed/filer/filerstore_translate_path.go.if_broken: Entries in a path-specific store come back with wrong paths, or land outside its root.
gotchas: Wrapping a translator in another translator returns the inner one unchanged, ignoring the new root.

weed/filer/filerstore_wrapper.go.character: The VirtualFilerStore every filer call goes through: routing to path-specific stores, hard links, chunk-id compaction, metrics and context detachment
weed/filer/filerstore_wrapper.go.what: FilerStoreWrapper routes each path to the default store or the path-specific store whose prefix matches, counts and times every operation, and on write moves chunk ids into the compact Fid form, maps the default mime to empty, strips ExtKeepRemoteObjectKey and maintains hard links; on read it restores ids and resolves hard links. Store calls run on a context detached from cancellation once started (a cancelled caller is refused only before the call). Prefix listing falls back to a client-side filter for stores without it. ScanEntries is offered only without path-specific stores. Transactions and KV always go to the default store. DeleteEntry and DeleteOneEntry decrement hard-link records unless the context marks a rename.
weed/filer/filerstore_wrapper.go.why: Consequence: a store write abandoned halfway because a client hung up could leave metadata inconsistent with what was already done around it (chunk deletes, events). Design: decide before the write, then finish it.
weed/filer/filerstore_wrapper.go.if_broken: Path-specific stores receive the wrong paths, hard links break, or chunk ids are lost in storage.
gotchas: Writes mutate the caller's entry in place: chunk FileId strings are moved into Fid (FileId cleared) and Extended loses ExtKeepRemoteObjectKey; a caller that reuses the entry afterwards sees the compacted chunks.
A hard-link record that cannot be read is logged and ignored by FindEntry, which returns the per-path entry without its shared data.
A FindEntry error on a whole-bucket-table store is turned into NotFound by matching the text 'Table' and "doesn't exist".

weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.character: An optional hook that overrides disk type, replication and data center per collection
weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.what: RegisterPlacementOverlay installs a factory; NewFiler builds the overlay from it if one is registered. ResolvePlacement asks it for a collection and reports whether it steered.
weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.why: Design: a seam for placement policy that is not expressed in filer.conf, without the filer core depending on it.
weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.when: The filer HTTP write path (filer_server_handlers_write.go) when choosing where to assign a chunk.
weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.ux: None unless an overlay is registered.
weed/filer/placement_overlay.go.if_broken: Writes ignore a configured placement policy.
gotchas: Nothing in this repository calls RegisterPlacementOverlay, so ResolvePlacement always reports no override here.

weed/filer/s3iam_conf.go.character: JSON helpers for the S3 and IAM configuration protos kept in the filer
weed/filer/s3iam_conf.go.what: ParseS3ConfigurationFromBytes unmarshals protojson leniently (unknown fields discarded, partial messages allowed); ProtoToText writes indented JSON with unpopulated fields; CheckDuplicateAccessKey refuses an access key configured on two different identities.
weed/filer/s3iam_conf.go.why: Design: the identity, circuit-breaker and other configs are stored as JSON protos in /etc so operators can edit them; lenient parsing lets older binaries read configs written by newer ones.
weed/filer/s3iam_conf.go.when: The S3 gateway loading /etc/iam and /etc/s3 files, the circuit breaker, shell commands that edit them.
weed/filer/s3iam_conf.go.if_broken: Configs fail to load, or two users share an access key.
gotchas: Unknown fields are discarded silently, so a misspelled field name in a hand-edited config is ignored rather than reported.
CheckDuplicateAccessKey checks identities only, not service accounts.

weed/filer/abstract_sql/.character: The shared implementation behind the MySQL, Postgres and SQLite filer stores, with optional one-table-per-bucket layout
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.what: AbstractSqlStore implements FilerStore on database/sql through a SqlGenerator each dialect supplies. Rows are keyed by (hash of directory, name, directory) with the encoded entry as the value (gzipped when it has more than 50 chunks on insert). With SupportBucketTable, paths under /buckets/<bucket>/ live in a table named after the bucket, created on first use and dropped when the bucket's children are deleted, so deleting a bucket is one DROP TABLE. Transactions are a *sql.Tx carried in the context under 'tx' (read committed). KV rows live in the default table, keyed by the first 8 bytes of the key and its base64 rest, optionally on a separate small connection pool (a quarter of max connections, at most 8). ScanEntries reads a subtree in one repeatable-read read-only transaction, across bucket tables when scanning / or /buckets, refusing when the store has a single connection. Retryable errors are retried outside transactions.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.why: Consequence: SQL stores are what multi-filer clusters share, so their key layout decides listing order and bucket-delete cost. Design: per-bucket tables make bucket deletion O(1) and keep one bucket's rows out of another's index; KV gets its own pool so a burst of metadata queries cannot starve lock and offset writes.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.when: Filers configured with mysql, mysql2, postgres, postgres2 or sqlite.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.ux: Fast bucket deletes with the per-bucket-table variants.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.if_broken: Entries vanish into the wrong table, bucket deletes leave rows, or the connection pool deadlocks.
gotchas: The bucket routing hardcodes /buckets/ instead of the filer's DirBucketsPath, and accepts bucket names by the lenient VerifyS3BucketName (non-ASCII names become table names).
Insert falls back to update only when the error text contains 'duplicate entry' (MySQL wording); KvPut falls back to update on any insert error.
UpdateEntry does not gzip large chunk lists the way InsertEntry does, and an UPDATE that matches no row reports success.
A transaction left open (see the StreamRenameEntry issue) keeps its pooled connection until the filer restarts, since the wrapper begins it on a context that is never cancelled.

weed/filer/filechunks.go.character: Chunk-list arithmetic: sizes, ETags, garbage detection, chunk differences and the chunk views a read needs
weed/filer/filechunks.go.what: TotalSize is the furthest chunk end; FileSize takes the larger of that and the stored size (and the remote size when the remote is newer). ETag returns the stored MD5, else ETagChunks: a single chunk's MD5, or the multipart form md5(concat(chunk md5s))-N. CompactFileChunks resolves manifests, computes visible intervals and splits chunks into those still visible and garbage fully overwritten by newer ones; MinusChunks resolves both lists (data and manifest chunks) and returns what the old list has that the new one does not, which is what the filer deletes on an update. ViewFromChunks / ViewFromVisibleIntervals cut the visible intervals into ChunkViews (file id, offset in chunk, view size and offset, cipher key, gzip flag) for a byte range; MergeIntoVisibles and MergeIntoChunkViews add one chunk to existing lists.
weed/filer/filechunks.go.why: Consequence: SeaweedFS files are lists of possibly overlapping chunks where the newest write wins; every read and every chunk deletion depends on computing which bytes of which chunk are visible.
